Former Vice-President Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan | Photo Credit: Senjuti Sengupta
India is facing challenges on several fronts which includes a gradual movement towards an authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Hamid Ansari said.
Mr. Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan, highlighted three point challenges faced by the country, which includes the pursuit of neoliberal policies, sharpening of communal polarisation and the movement towards authoritarian rule.
“This threefold attack includes the aggressive pursuit of neoliberal policies of economic reforms. Secondly, the relentless onslaught on the secular democratic foundations of the Indian republic by sharpening of communal polarisation, and thirdly, the movement towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions and methods of which are considered sacrosanct in a democracy,” the former Vice-President said.
From Sept 2026: Former V-P Hamid Ansari’s remarks exposed ‘Muslim League-Maoist character’ of Congress, says BJP
Recalling the contribution of the late Sitaram Yechury. Mr Ansari said that the CPI(M) spoke against the certain ideological position in which nationalism has only been equated with Hindu nationalism.
“Bharat Mata has no Hinduism in naturalism. This is not a Bharat Mata that has given birth to Muslims, Christians, Tarsus, Buddhists, Jains, and atheists,” Mr. Ansari quoted Mr. Yechury from one of his speeches in 2017.
The former Vice-President also said Mr. Yechury opined that the struggle against imperialist aggression, the imposition of neoliberal order, and fundamentalism should be welded together to form a powerful anti-imperialist movement. He emphasised the need to maintain multilateralism in external affairs so as not to compromise on foreign policy positions,
Mr. Ansari recalled that Mr. Yechury, despite some frictions within the CPI(M) and with the Congress, formed a strong relationship with the Congress leadership, particularly with Sonia Gandhi and the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi. He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government.
He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. This is usually strange. The Congress accepted many of the suggestions to ensure a working majority,” he added.
Meanwhile, general secretary of CPI(M) M.A. Baby, Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera, renowned economist Prabhat Patnaik, historian Mukul Kesavan, and distinguished scholar Malini Bhattacharya were also present in the seminar in Kolkata on Sunday (November 22, 2026).
Addressing the seminar, Mr. Baby said that imperialism has reached a diabolical and barbaric stage across the world today. “Before Israel was to launch an attack on Iran without any rhyme or reason, the Prime Minister of India goes to Israel and addresses the Israeli Parliament two days ahead oftime. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism.
In his lecture, Mr. Patnaik discussed the current problems of capitalism, and called capitalism the basis of imperialism. He said that imperialism now looks so desperate and is causing an international crisis for which we still don’t have a clear answer. But he viewed the problems of capitalism are reasons behind such desperation.
“The U.S. is trying to capture and acquire control over the entire world’s oil resources. In order to buy oil futures, they have to pay dollars. So, the demand for dollars cannot drop much “ He argued to show the USA’s desperation to capture the world’s precious resources through a recolonisation process.
The Cuban Ambassador recalled Mr. Yechury’s contribution to strengthening India’s ties to Cuba. “He publicly reaffirmed his support to the Cuban people, recalling the difficult circumstances Cuba faced during the special period after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the resilience of the Cuban people and the role of the Communist Party of Cuba in building the unity that has ensured popular support to the revolution,” he said.
